# Spatial statistics

## plotRipleyCrossK

Plot Ripley's cross K against distance.

`plotRipleyCrossK` plots the observed cross K, with the simulation envelope if there is one.

```r
plotRipleyCrossK(
  kcross,
  title = NULL,
  observed_color = "black",
  simulated_color = "grey30",
  envelope_fill = "grey75",
  envelope_alpha = 0.45,
  facet = TRUE,
  log_y = FALSE
)
```

Arguments:

- `kcross`: Result of [`spatialRipleyCrossK()`](spatialRipleyCrossK.md).
- `title`: Plot title.
- `observed_color`: Color of the observed curve.
- `simulated_color`: Color of the dotted simulated curve.
- `envelope_fill`: Fill color of the simulation envelope.
- `envelope_alpha`: Opacity of the simulation envelope.
- `facet`: Make one panel for each image if the result has several images (default `TRUE`)?
- `log_y`: Use a log10 scale for the y-axis (default `FALSE`)?

Value: A ggplot object.

## plotSpatialCloneJoinCount

Plot a clone join-count result.

`plotSpatialCloneJoinCount` plots the tissue map of one tested clone. It also shows the observed and expected number of joins between spots of the same clone.

```r
plotSpatialCloneJoinCount(
  join_count,
  object,
  clone_val,
  images = NULL,
  sample_id = NULL,
  polygon_val = NULL,
  polygon = NULL,
  image_scale = NULL,
  swap_coords = NULL,
  show_neighbors = TRUE,
  clone_color = "#D55E00",
  other_color = "grey75",
  point_size = 1.8,
  point_alpha = 0.9,
  edge_width = 0.6,
  edge_alpha = 0.75,
  polygon_color = "black",
  polygon_linewidth = 0.6,
  image_alpha = 1,
  zoom = FALSE,
  title = NULL,
  combine_sample_plots = FALSE
)
```

Arguments:

- `join_count`: Result of [`spatialCloneJoinCount()`](spatialCloneJoinCount.md). Run that function with `return_data = TRUE`.
- `object`: Seurat object with spatial images, or a SIRUP object.
- `clone_val`: Clone ID to plot.
- `images`: Names of the images to plot.
- `sample_id`: Names of the samples to plot. Use it for multi-sample SIRUP objects. If `NULL`, the function plots all samples.
- `polygon_val`: IDs of the polygons to include.
- `polygon`: Data frame of polygon vertices to draw on the tissue.
- `image_scale`: Image scale for `SeuratObject::GetTissueCoordinates()`. If `NULL`, the function uses the value stored in the SIRUP object.
- `swap_coords`: Swap the two Seurat coordinate axes? If `NULL`, the function uses the value stored in the SIRUP object.
- `show_neighbors`: Draw a line between each pair of neighboring spots that both contain the clone (default `TRUE`)?
- `clone_color`: Color of the spots and lines for the clone.
- `other_color`: Color of the other spots that have receptors.
- `point_size`: Size of the spots.
- `point_alpha`: Opacity of the spots.
- `edge_width`: Width of the neighbor lines.
- `edge_alpha`: Opacity of the neighbor lines.
- `polygon_color`: Color of the polygon outlines.
- `polygon_linewidth`: Width of the polygon outlines.
- `image_alpha`: Opacity of the tissue image.
- `zoom`: Zoom to the spots in the test (default `FALSE`)?
- `title`: Title of the combined plot.
- `combine_sample_plots`: Combine the plots of all samples into one figure (default `FALSE`)? The function uses it only for multi-sample objects. If `FALSE`, it returns a named list with one plot for each sample.

Value: A ggplot object. For a multi-sample object and `combine_sample_plots = FALSE`, a named list of plots.

## plotSpatialLocalMoran

Plot local Moran's I on a tissue image.

`plotSpatialLocalMoran` colors each spot by its local Moran\'s I result.

```r
plotSpatialLocalMoran(
  object,
  local_moran,
  value_col = "z_i",
  images = NULL,
  sample_id = NULL,
  image_scale = NULL,
  swap_coords = NULL,
  colors = c("#2c7bb6", "#f7f7f7", "#d7191c"),
  midpoint = 0,
  point_size = 0.7,
  point_alpha = 1,
  order_points = TRUE,
  image_alpha = 1,
  zoom = FALSE,
  title = NULL,
  combine = TRUE,
  combine_sample_plots = FALSE
)
```

Arguments:

- `object`: SIRUP object, or Seurat object with spatial images.
- `local_moran`: Result of [`spatialLocalMoran()`](spatialLocalMoran.md).
- `value_col`: Name of the column to color by (default `"z_i"`).
- `images`: Names of the Seurat images to use.
- `sample_id`: Names of the samples to plot. Use it for multi-sample SIRUP objects. If `NULL`, the function plots all samples.
- `image_scale`: Image scale for `SeuratObject::GetTissueCoordinates()`. If `NULL`, the function uses the value stored in the SIRUP object.
- `swap_coords`: Swap the two Seurat coordinate axes? If `NULL`, the function uses the value stored in the SIRUP object. Give a value if `object` is a Seurat object.
- `colors`: Three colors for the low, middle, and high values.
- `midpoint`: Value that gets the middle color.
- `point_size`: Size of the spots.
- `point_alpha`: Opacity of the spots.
- `order_points`: Draw low values first, so that high values show on top (default `TRUE`)?
- `image_alpha`: Opacity of the tissue image.
- `zoom`: Zoom to the plotted spots (default `FALSE`)?
- `title`: Plot title.
- `combine`: Combine the image panels with patchwork (default `TRUE`)?
- `combine_sample_plots`: Combine the plots of all samples into one patchwork (default `FALSE`)? The function uses it only for multi-sample objects. If `FALSE`, it returns a named list with one plot for each sample.

Value: A ggplot or patchwork object.

## spatialCloneJoinCount

Test clone localization with join counts.

`spatialCloneJoinCount` tests if each clone clusters in space.

```r
spatialCloneJoinCount(
  object,
  receptors = NULL,
  clone = NULL,
  spatial_id = NULL,
  clone_val = NULL,
  polygon = NULL,
  polygon_val = NULL,
  images = NULL,
  image_scale = NULL,
  swap_coords = NULL,
  x = "x",
  y = "y",
  polygon_id = "polygon",
  include_boundary = TRUE,
  min_spatial_ids = 2,
  radius = NULL,
  k = 6,
  alternative = "greater",
  other_label = "Other",
  use_stored_polygons = NULL,
  return_data = FALSE,
  slot = NULL
)
```

Arguments:

- `object`: Seurat object or SIRUP object.
- `receptors`: AIRR-style receptor table with spatial IDs and clone IDs. Omit if `object` is a SIRUP object.
- `clone`: Name of the `receptors` column that holds the clone IDs. If `object` is a SIRUP object and this argument is `NULL`, the function uses the stored clone field, if there is one.
- `spatial_id`: Name of the `receptors` column that holds the spatial IDs. If `object` is a SIRUP object and this argument is `NULL`, the function uses the stored spatial ID field. Give a value if you use separate Seurat and receptor objects.
- `clone_val`: Clone IDs to test. If `NULL`, the function tests all clones that occur in at least `min_spatial_ids` spatial IDs.
- `polygon`: Data frame of polygon vertices. The function tests only the spots inside these polygons (default `NULL`).
- `polygon_val`: Polygon IDs to select from `polygon`.
- `images`: Names of the Seurat images to use.
- `image_scale`: Image scale for `SeuratObject::GetTissueCoordinates()`. If `NULL`, the function uses the value stored in the SIRUP object.
- `swap_coords`: Swap the two Seurat coordinate axes? If `NULL`, the function uses the value stored in the SIRUP object. Give a value if `object` is a Seurat object.
- `x`: Name of the x-coordinate column in `polygon` (default `"x"`).
- `y`: Name of the y-coordinate column in `polygon` (default `"y"`).
- `polygon_id`: Name of the column in `polygon` that groups the vertices by polygon (default `"polygon"`).
- `include_boundary`: Count spots on a polygon edge as inside the polygon (default `TRUE`)? The function ignores this argument if `object` is a SIRUP object with stored polygons and `polygon` is `NULL`. In that case, it uses the stored polygon annotations.
- `min_spatial_ids`: Smallest number of spatial IDs that a clone needs to be tested (default 2).
- `radius`: Distance that defines a neighborhood. If `NULL`, the function uses `k`.
- `k`: Number of nearest neighbors, used if `radius` is `NULL` (default 6).
- `alternative`: Alternative hypothesis for `spdep::joincount.test()` (default `"greater"`).
- `other_label`: Label for the spatial IDs that do not contain the tested clone (default `"Other"`).
- `use_stored_polygons`: Run one test for each stored polygon of a SIRUP object? Use `TRUE` to require stored polygons. Use `FALSE` to build one neighbor graph for each sample and ignore stored polygons. If `NULL` (default), the function uses `TRUE` when a SIRUP object has stored polygons and you give no `polygon`. Otherwise, it uses `FALSE`.
- `return_data`: Return the data used for each test (default `FALSE`)?
- `slot`: Name of the receptor slot to use. Leave it `NULL` if the SIRUP object has one receptor table. You must give it if the object has several slots and the function reads receptors. The function ignores `slot` if you give a plain receptor table.

Value: A list with these items: `summary` (a table with one row for each tested clone and region, ordered by p-value), `tests` (the `spdep` test results), `data` (the data for each test, or `NULL` if `return_data` is `FALSE`), `neighbors`, `weights`, `radius`, `k`, `alternative`, and `min_spatial_ids`.

## spatialCloneSpread

Summarize the spatial spread of clones.

`spatialCloneSpread` gives the distances between the spots of each clone in each sample.

```r
spatialCloneSpread(
  object,
  receptors = NULL,
  clone = NULL,
  spatial_id = NULL,
  clone_val = NULL,
  images = NULL,
  image_scale = NULL,
  swap_coords = NULL,
  min_spatial_ids = 2L,
  collapse_within_spot = FALSE,
  slot = NULL
)
```

Arguments:

- `object`: SIRUP object, or Seurat object with spatial images. For a Seurat object, give `receptors`.
- `receptors`: AIRR-style receptor table. Omit it if `object` is a SIRUP object.
- `clone`: Name of the column that holds the clone IDs. If `NULL`, the function uses the stored clone field of a SIRUP object, if there is one.
- `spatial_id`: Name of the column that holds the spatial IDs. If `NULL`, the function uses the stored spatial ID field of a SIRUP object.
- `clone_val`: Clone IDs to keep.
- `images`: Names of the images or samples to include.
- `image_scale`: Image scale for the Seurat image coordinates.
- `swap_coords`: Swap the x and y coordinates before the function calculates distances?
- `min_spatial_ids`: Smallest number of observations that a clone needs in a sample (default 2). If `collapse_within_spot` is `TRUE`, the function counts distinct spots. Otherwise, it counts sequences.
- `collapse_within_spot`: Merge the sequences that share a spatial ID into one point before the function calculates distances (default `FALSE`)? If `FALSE`, the function counts every sequence, so sequences in the same spot give pairs with distance zero. Use `TRUE` to measure the spread over distinct spots only.
- `slot`: Name of the receptor slot to use. Leave it `NULL` if the SIRUP object has one receptor table. You must give it if the object has several slots and the function reads receptors. The function ignores `slot` if you give a plain receptor table.

Value: A tibble with one row for each sample and clone. The columns are `sample`, `clone_id`, `n_spatial_ids`, `mean_pairwise_distance`, and `max_pairwise_distance`.

## spatialCoordinateExtents

Summarize spatial coordinate ranges.

`spatialCoordinateExtents` gives the x and y range of each sample or image.

```r
spatialCoordinateExtents(
  object,
  by = c("sample", "image"),
  images = NULL,
  image_scale = NULL,
  swap_coords = NULL
)
```

Arguments:

- `object`: SIRUP object, or Seurat object with spatial images.
- `by`: Group the ranges by `sample` or by `image`.
- `images`: Names of the images or samples to include.
- `image_scale`: Image scale for the Seurat image coordinates.
- `swap_coords`: Swap the x and y coordinates?

Value: A tibble with the ranges (`x_min`, `x_max`, `y_min`, `y_max`), the `width`, `height`, and `diagonal`, and the number of spots (`n_spatial_ids`).

## spatialCoordinateTable

Get spatial plotting coordinates.

`spatialCoordinateTable` returns the coordinate table that SIRUP uses for spatial statistics and plots.

```r
spatialCoordinateTable(
  object,
  images = NULL,
  image_scale = NULL,
  swap_coords = NULL
)
```

Arguments:

- `object`: Seurat object.
- `images`: Names of the images to include.
- `image_scale`: Image scale for the Seurat image coordinates.
- `swap_coords`: Swap the x and y coordinates?

Value: A data frame with at least these columns: `cell`, `x`, `y`, `.sirup_y`, and `image`.

## spatialLee

Calculate global Lee's L.

`spatialLee` tests the spatial association between two continuous variables.

```r
spatialLee(
  object,
  x,
  y,
  x_type = c("feature", "metadata"),
  y_type = c("feature", "metadata"),
  assay = NULL,
  layer = "counts",
  images = NULL,
  image_scale = NULL,
  swap_coords = NULL,
  radius = NULL,
  k = 6,
  alternative = "greater",
  method = c("analytical", "mc"),
  nsim = 999,
  progress = FALSE
)
```

Arguments:

- `object`: Seurat object or SIRUP object.
- `x`: Name of the first variable. It is a feature or a numeric metadata column.
- `y`: Name of the second variable. It is a feature or a numeric metadata column.
- `x_type`: Type of `x`: `feature` or `metadata`.
- `y_type`: Type of `y`: `feature` or `metadata`.
- `assay`: Assay to use if `x_type` or `y_type` is `"feature"`.
- `layer`: Seurat expression layer to use for features (default `"counts"`).
- `images`: Names of the Seurat images to use.
- `image_scale`: Image scale for `SeuratObject::GetTissueCoordinates()`. If `NULL`, the function uses the value stored in the SIRUP object.
- `swap_coords`: Swap the two Seurat coordinate axes? If `NULL`, the function uses the value stored in the SIRUP object. Give a value if `object` is a Seurat object.
- `radius`: Distance that defines a neighborhood. If `NULL`, the function uses `k`.
- `k`: Number of nearest neighbors, used if `radius` is `NULL` (default 6). Use `k = 8` for Visium HD, where the bins form a square grid. Use `k = 6` for standard Visium, where the spots form a hexagonal grid.
- `alternative`: Alternative hypothesis for the significance test (default `"greater"`).
- `method`: Significance test: `analytical` or `mc` (permutation). See Details.
- `nsim`: Number of permutations for `method = "mc"` (default 999).
- `progress`: Show a progress bar for the permutations (default `FALSE`)? The function uses it only if `method = "mc"`. Each permutation re-lags both variables over every spot. For Visium HD, a large `nsim` takes minutes for each pair.

Value: A list with these items: `test` (the test result), `L` (the observed Lee\'s L), `method`, `data` (the values tested), `neighbors` and `weights` (from `spdep`), `radius`, `k`, `x`, `y`, `x_type`, and `y_type`.

## spatialLocalMoran

Calculate local Moran's I (LISA).

`spatialLocalMoran` calculates local Moran\'s I for each spot. It shows where high or low values cluster.

```r
spatialLocalMoran(
  object,
  variable,
  variable_type = c("feature", "metadata", "receptor", "clone"),
  value = NULL,
  receptors = NULL,
  spatial_id = NULL,
  clone = NULL,
  assay = NULL,
  layer = "counts",
  images = NULL,
  image_scale = NULL,
  swap_coords = NULL,
  radius = NULL,
  k = 6,
  slot = NULL
)
```

Arguments:

- `object`: Seurat object or SIRUP object.
- `variable`: Name of the feature or the metadata column to test.
- `variable_type`: Type of `variable`: `feature` (gene expression), `metadata` (Seurat metadata column), `receptor` (receptor table column), or `clone` (clone ID).
- `value`: Metadata value to convert to a 0/1 indicator (default `NULL`).
- `receptors`: AIRR-style receptor table. You must give it if `variable_type` is `"receptor"` or `"clone"` and `object` is not a SIRUP object.
- `spatial_id`: Name of the `receptors` column that holds the spatial IDs. If `object` is a SIRUP object and this argument is `NULL`, the function uses the stored spatial ID field. Give a value if you use separate Seurat and receptor objects.
- `clone`: Name of the `receptors` column that holds the clone IDs. The function uses it only if `variable_type` is `"clone"`. If `object` is a SIRUP object and this argument is `NULL`, the function uses the stored clone field, if there is one.
- `assay`: Assay to use if `variable_type` is `"feature"`.
- `layer`: Seurat expression layer to use for features (default `"counts"`).
- `images`: Names of the Seurat images to use.
- `image_scale`: Image scale for `SeuratObject::GetTissueCoordinates()`. If `NULL`, the function uses the value stored in the SIRUP object.
- `swap_coords`: Swap the two Seurat coordinate axes? If `NULL`, the function uses the value stored in the SIRUP object. Give a value if `object` is a Seurat object.
- `radius`: Distance that defines a neighborhood. If `NULL`, the function uses the `k` nearest neighbors.
- `k`: Number of nearest neighbors, used if `radius` is `NULL` (default 6).
- `slot`: Name of the receptor slot to use. Leave it `NULL` if the SIRUP object has one receptor table. You must give it if the object has several slots and the function reads receptors. The function ignores `slot` if you give a plain receptor table.

Value: A data frame with the coordinates, the values, local Moran\'s I, the z-scores, and the p-values.

## spatialMoran

Calculate global Moran's I.

`spatialMoran` tests one variable for spatial autocorrelation across spots using Moran\'s I.

```r
spatialMoran(
  object,
  variable,
  variable_type = c("feature", "metadata", "receptor", "clone"),
  value = NULL,
  receptors = NULL,
  spatial_id = NULL,
  clone = NULL,
  assay = NULL,
  layer = "counts",
  images = NULL,
  image_scale = NULL,
  swap_coords = NULL,
  radius = NULL,
  k = 6,
  alternative = "greater",
  slot = NULL
)
```

Arguments:

- `object`: Seurat object or SIRUP object.
- `variable`: Name of the feature or the metadata column to test.
- `variable_type`: Type of `variable`: `feature` (gene expression), `metadata` (Seurat metadata column), `receptor` (receptor table column), or `clone` (clone ID).
- `value`: Metadata value to convert to a 0/1 indicator (default `NULL`).
- `receptors`: AIRR-style receptor table. You must give it if `variable_type` is `"receptor"` or `"clone"` and `object` is not a SIRUP object.
- `spatial_id`: Name of the `receptors` column that holds the spatial IDs. If `object` is a SIRUP object and this argument is `NULL`, the function uses the stored spatial ID field. Give a value if you use separate Seurat and receptor objects.
- `clone`: Name of the `receptors` column that holds the clone IDs. The function uses it only if `variable_type` is `"clone"`. If `object` is a SIRUP object and this argument is `NULL`, the function uses the stored clone field, if there is one.
- `assay`: Assay to use if `variable_type` is `"feature"`.
- `layer`: Seurat expression layer to use for features (default `"counts"`).
- `images`: Names of the Seurat images to use.
- `image_scale`: Image scale for `SeuratObject::GetTissueCoordinates()`. If `NULL`, the function uses the value stored in the SIRUP object.
- `swap_coords`: Swap the two Seurat coordinate axes? If `NULL`, the function uses the value stored in the SIRUP object. Give a value if `object` is a Seurat object.
- `radius`: Distance that defines a neighborhood. If `NULL`, the function uses `k`.
- `k`: Number of nearest neighbors, used if `radius` is `NULL` (default 6).
- `alternative`: Alternative hypothesis for `spdep::moran.test()` (default `"greater"`).
- `slot`: Name of the receptor slot to use. Leave it `NULL` if the SIRUP object has one receptor table. You must give it if the object has several slots and the function reads receptors. The function ignores `slot` if you give a plain receptor table.

Value: For one image, a list with these items: `test` (the `spdep::moran.test()` result), `data` (the values tested), `neighbors` and `weights` (from `spdep`), `radius`, `k`, and `variable`. For several images, the list has `tests`, `neighbors`, and `weights` as named lists with one entry for each image. It also has `summary`, a data frame with one row for each image (`image`, `statistic`, `p_value`, `moran_i`, `expectation`, `variance`), and the items `data`, `radius`, `k`, and `variable`.

## spatialRipleyCrossK

Calculate Ripley's cross K.

`spatialRipleyCrossK` measures how spots of mark `i` cluster around spots of mark `j` at different distances. Similar to Lee\'s L but better for factor data.

```r
spatialRipleyCrossK(
  object,
  mark_col,
  i,
  j,
  nsim = 0,
  max_r = NULL,
  r = NULL,
  image_scale = NULL,
  swap_coords = NULL
)
```

Arguments:

- `object`: Seurat object or SIRUP object.
- `mark_col`: Name of the metadata column that holds the point types.
- `i`: First mark level.
- `j`: Second mark level.
- `nsim`: Number of random-label simulations for the envelope (default 0). Use `0` for the observed K only.
- `max_r`: Largest radius to calculate. The function ignores it if you give `r`.
- `r`: Vector of distances for `spatstat.explore::Kcross()`.
- `image_scale`: Image scale for `SeuratObject::GetTissueCoordinates()`. If `NULL`, the function uses the value stored in the SIRUP object.
- `swap_coords`: Swap the two Seurat coordinate axes? If `NULL`, the function uses the value stored in the SIRUP object. Give a value if `object` is a Seurat object.

Value: A list with these items: `observed` (the observed K), `envelope` (the simulation envelope, if any), `plot_data`, `points` (the point data), `i`, `j`, `correction`, `nsim`, `max_r`, and `r`.
